title: The Launderer
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: This occupational designation appears several times with the sages of Israel in the time of the Tannaim.
In Berakhot 28a, when Rabban Gamliel was reconciled with Rabbi Yehoshua, they said: “Who will go and tell the Rabbis?” A certain launderer said to them: “I will go.”

In Sanhedrin 38b, when the Sadducee asked Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose: It is written, “And the Lord rained … from the Lord” — it should have said “from Him”! — a certain launderer said to him: “Leave him; I will answer him, for it is written,” etc. He said to him: “From where do you have this?” He said: “I heard it from Rabbi Meir’s lecture.”

In Nedarim 41a: when Rabbi learned thirteen versions of the halakhah, he taught Rabbi Chiyya seven of them. In the end Rabbi fell ill; Rabbi Chiyya reviewed before him the seven versions he had taught him, but six were lost. There was a certain kassra (launderer, according to Rashi) who used to hear Rabbi as he studied them; Rabbi Chiyya went and learned them before the launderer … Rabbi said to him: “You have made me and Chiyya.”

Ketubot 103b relates that on the day of Rabbi’s funeral a heavenly voice went out and said: “Whoever was present at Rabbi’s funeral is destined for the life of the world to come.” A certain launderer used to come before him every day; that day he did not come. When he heard this, he went up to the roof, fell to the ground and died. A heavenly voice went out and said: “That launderer too is destined for the life of the world to come.”

notes.text: אשכבתיה is Rabbi’s funeral, not attendance at the instant of death. These are several notices of an occupation, not proof of one launderer’s identity across the stories. יהשוע/כובד are read as יהושע/כובס, and the Nedarim thirteen/seven/six account is retained without new omitted dialogue.

The consulted Nedarim 41a directly preserves thirteen versions, seven taught to Chiyya and six recovered through the launderer, followed by two versions of Rabbi’s acknowledgment. The occupational notices are not merged as one person, and omitted dialogue is not inserted into Hyman’s abridgment. The funeral correction in the current note remains verbatim.
